title: حِكَايَةُ الْعَاشِقِ وَالْمَعْشُوقِ
titleEn: The Lover and the Beloved, continued
part: Night 123 · The Lover and the Beloved, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 597–599 (Night 123, continuing directly from nights-122), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 123 continues the story that the vizier Dandān tells within the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, the story of the lover, the beloved and the go-between. ʿAzīz goes on with his tale to Tāj al-Mulūk. Locked inside the house, he is seized by the young woman and carried through seven passages into a marble hall, where she offers him a choice between death and marriage. She knows the lady he has been visiting — “the daughter of Dalīla the trickster” — and tells him that his dead cousin ʿAzīza’s parting words are what kept him alive. Then, frankly and with much laughter, she says what she wants of a husband, and the old woman brings in witnesses for the marriage contract. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ وَالْعِشْرُونَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thālithatu wa-al-ʿishrūna baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the third and the twenty after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and twenty-third night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ الشَّابَّ عَزِيزْ قَالَ لِتَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ فَلَمَّا دَفَعَتْنِي الْعَجُوزُ لَمْ أَشْعُرْ إِلَّا وَأَنَا مِنْ دَاخِلِ الدِّهْلِيزِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-shābba ʿazīz qāla li-tāji al-mulūki fa-lammā dafaʿatnī al-ʿajūzu lam ashʿur illā wa-anā min dākhili al-dihlīzi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the youth ʿAzīz said to Tāj al-Mulūk: And when the old-woman pushed me, I did not perceive except that I (was) from inside the passage.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the young man ʿAzīz said to Tāj al-Mulūk: When the old woman pushed me, before I knew it I was inside the entrance passage.
sentences.n: The print runs al-saʿīdu and anna together as one word, and gives the name ʿAzīz without the alif of the accusative, so it is read here without a case ending. lam ashʿur illā wa-anā …, “I did not perceive, except that I …”, is the idiom for something that happens before one knows it. A dihlīz is the passage that leads from a house’s street door to its inner rooms.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَتِ الْعَجُوزَةُ أَسْرَعَ مِنَ الْبَرْقِ الْخَاطِفِ وَمَا كَانَ لَهَا شُغْلٌ إِلَّاقَفْلُ الْبَابِ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhalati al-ʿajūzatu asraʿa mina al-barqi al-khāṭifi wa-mā kāna lahā shughlun illā qaflu al-bābi
sentences.l: And the old-woman entered, faster than the lightning, the snatching, and there was not for her a business except the locking of the door.
sentences.i: The old woman came in after me quicker than a flash of lightning, and her only care was to lock the door.
sentences.n: al-ʿajūza: the print gives the old woman a feminine ending, a spoken form; the book word ʿajūz is feminine without it. al-barq al-khāṭif, “the snatching lightning”, the lightning that takes away the sight, is a stock image of speed. The print runs illā and qafl together as one word.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الصَّبِيَّةُ فَإِنَّهَا لَمَّا رَأَتْنِي مِنْ دَاخِلِ الدِّهْلِيزِ أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيَّ وَضَمَّتْنِي إِلَى صَدْرِهَا وَرَمَتْنِي عَلَى الْأَرْضِ وَرَكِبَتْ عَلَى صَدْرِي وَعَصَرَتْ بَطْنِي بِيَدَيْهَا فَغِبْتُ عَنِ الدُّنْيَا
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-ṣabiyyatu fa-innahā lammā raʾatnī min dākhili al-dihlīzi aqbalat ʿalayya wa-ḍammatnī ilā ṣadrihā wa-ramatnī ʿalā al-arḍi wa-rakibat ʿalā ṣadrī wa-ʿaṣarat baṭnī bi-yadayhā fa-ghibtu ʿani al-dunyā
sentences.l: And as for the young-woman, then she, when she saw me from inside the passage, came-forward upon me and pressed me to her breast, and threw me on the ground, and rode upon my chest, and squeezed my belly with her two hands, so I was-absent from the world.
sentences.i: As for the young woman, when she saw me inside the passage she came at me, clasped me to her breast, threw me to the ground, sat astride my chest and squeezed my belly with both hands until I lost my senses.
sentences.n: The print has اقبلب, a misprint for اقبلت (aqbalat, “she came towards”), corrected here. bi-yadayhā, “with her two hands”: bi- of the instrument. ghibtu ʿani al-dunyā, “I was absent from the world”, is to faint.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذَتْنِي بِيَدِهَا فَمَا قَدَرْتُ أَنْ أَتَخَلَّصَ مِنْهَا مِنْ شِدَّةِ مَا حَضَنَتْنِي ثُمَّ دَخَلَتْ بِي وَالْعَجُوزُ قُدَّامَهَا وَالشَّمْعَةُ مَوْقُودَةٌ مَعَهَا حَتَّى قَطَعَتْ بِي سَبْعَ دَهَالِيزَ
sentences.tr: thumma akhadhatnī bi-yadihā fa-mā qadartu an atakhallaṣa minhā min shiddati mā ḥaḍanatnī thumma dakhalat bī wa-al-ʿajūzu quddāmahā wa-al-shamʿatu mawqūdatun maʿahā ḥattā qaṭaʿat bī sabʿa dahālīza
sentences.l: Then she took me by her hand, and I was not able to free-myself from her, from the intensity of what she hugged me; then she entered with me, and the old-woman before her and the candle lit with her, until she crossed with me seven passages.
sentences.i: Then she took me by the hand, and she held me so tightly that I could not get free of her. She led me in, with the old woman going ahead carrying the lighted candle, and took me through seven passages.
sentences.n: dakhalat bī, “she entered with me”: bi- with a verb of motion means taking someone along, so “she led me in”; qaṭaʿat bī, “she crossed with me”, works the same way. min shiddati mā ḥaḍanatnī, “from the force of her hugging me”: mā turns the verb into a noun. dahālīz, plural of dihlīz, takes -a in the genitive.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَخَلَتْ بِي إِلَى قَاعَةٍ كَبِيرَةٍ بِأَرْبَعَةِ لَوَاوِينَ يَلْعَبُ فِيهَا الْخَيَّالُ بِالْاُكَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika dakhalat bī ilā qāʿatin kabīratin bi-arbaʿati lawāwīna yalʿabu fīhā al-khayyālu bi-al-ukari
sentences.l: And after that she entered with me into a hall, big, with four līwāns, the horseman plays in it with the balls.
sentences.i: After that she brought me into a great hall with four alcoves, so wide that a horseman could play at ball in it.
sentences.n: A qāʿa is the great reception hall of a fine house; a līwān is one of the raised, open-fronted recesses round its central floor, and lawāwīn is the spoken plural. bi-arbaʿati, “with four”: bi- of what a thing has. yalʿabu fīhā al-khayyālu bi-al-ukari, “the horseman plays in it with the balls”, is a boast of size: a rider could play the mounted ball game there. The print itself sets the ḍamma on the alif of ukar.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَلَّتْنِي وَقَالَتْ لِي افْتَحْ عَيْنَيْكَ فَفَتَحْتُ عَيْنِي وَأَنَا دَائِخٌ مِنْ شِدَّةِ مَا ضَمَّتْنِي وَعَصَرَتْنِي
sentences.tr: thumma khallatnī wa-qālat lī iftaḥ ʿaynayka fa-fataḥtu ʿaynī wa-anā dāʾikhun min shiddati mā ḍammatnī wa-ʿaṣaratnī
sentences.l: Then she let-me-go and said to me: Open your two eyes. So I opened my eye, and I (was) dizzy from the intensity of what she pressed me and squeezed me.
sentences.i: Then she let me go and said, “Open your eyes.” I opened them, dizzy from the way she had clasped and squeezed me.
sentences.n: khallatnī, “she let me go”, from khallā, to leave alone. dāʾikh, “dizzy”, is a spoken word.

sentences.t: فَرَأَيْتُ بِنَاءَ الْقَاعَةِ كُلُّهَا رُخَامٌ مِنْ أَبْهَجِ الْمَرْمَرِ وَجَمِيعُ فَرْشِهَا مِنْ حَرِيرٍ وَدِيبَاجٍ وَكَذَلِكَ الْمِخَدَّاتُ وَالْمَرَاتِبُ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾaytu bināʾa al-qāʿati kulluhā rukhāmun min abhaji al-marmari wa-jamīʿu farshihā min ḥarīrin wa-dībājin wa-ka-dhālika al-mikhaddātu wa-al-marātibu
sentences.l: And I saw the building of the hall: all of it marble, of the most-delightful of the alabaster, and all of its furnishing of silk and brocade, and like-that the cushions and the mattresses.
sentences.i: I saw that the whole hall was built of marble, of the loveliest white kind, and all its furnishings were of silk and brocade, and so were the cushions and the mattresses.
sentences.n: kulluhā rukhāmun, “all of it marble”, is a clause of its own, saying what he saw. marmar is fine white marble or alabaster. ka-dhālika, “like that”: ka- is “like”.

sentences.t: وَهُنَاكَ دَكَّتَانِ مِنَ النُّحَاسِ الْأَصْفَرِ وَسَرِيرٌ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ الْأَحْمَرِ مُرَصَّعٌ بِالدُّرِّ وَالْجَوْهَرِ وَمَقَاعِدُ وَبَيْتُ سَعَادَةٍ لَايَصْلُحُ إِلَّا لِلْمَلِكِ مِثْلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-hunāka dakkatāni mina al-nuḥāsi al-aṣfari wa-sarīrun mina al-dhahabi al-aḥmari muraṣṣaʿun bi-al-durri wa-al-jawhari wa-maqāʿidu wa-baytu saʿādatin lā-yaṣluḥu illā li-al-maliki mithlika
sentences.l: And there (were) two benches of the copper, the yellow, and a couch of the gold, the red, inlaid with the pearl and the jewel, and seats, and a house of felicity, (which) is not fitting except for the king like you.
sentences.i: There were two benches of brass and a couch of red gold set with pearls and gems, and seats, and a house of good fortune fit only for a king like you.
sentences.n: A dakka is a raised bench; al-nuḥās al-aṣfar, “yellow copper”, is brass. al-dhahab al-aḥmar, “red gold”, is pure gold. muraṣṣaʿun bi-, “inlaid with”: bi- names the inlay. mithlika, “like you”: ʿAzīz turns aside to his listener, Tāj al-Mulūk. The print runs lā and yaṣluḥu together.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لِي يَا عَزِيزُ أَيُّمَا أَحَبُّ إِلَيْكَ الْمَوْتُ أَمِ الْحَيَاةُ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lī yā ʿazīzu ayyumā aḥabbu ilayka al-mawtu ami al-ḥayātu
sentences.l: Then she said to me: O ʿAzīz, which-ever (is) more-beloved to you, the death or the life?
sentences.i: Then she said to me, “ʿAzīz, which would you rather have, death or life?”

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا الْحَيَاةُ فَقَالَتْ لِي إِذَا كَانَتِ الْحَيَوٰةُ أَحَبَّ إِلَيْكَ فَتَزَوَّجْ بِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā al-ḥayātu fa-qālat lī idhā kānati al-ḥayātu aḥabba ilayka fa-tazawwaj bī
sentences.l: So I said to her: The life. So she said to me: If the life is more-beloved to you, then marry with me.
sentences.i: “Life,” I said. She said, “If life is dearer to you, then marry me.”
sentences.n: The print spells al-ḥayāt the second time in the old Qurʾānic way, الحيوة, with wāw for the long ā. tazawwaja bi-, “to marry (someone)”: the verb takes the spouse with bi-.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ أَنَا أَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَتَزَوَّجَ بِمِثْلِكِ فَقَالَتْ لِي إِنْ تَزَوَّجْتَ بِي تَسْلَمْ مِنْ بِنْتِ الدَّلِيلَةِ الْمُحْتَالَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu anā akrahu an atazawwaja bi-mithliki fa-qālat lī in tazawwajta bī taslam min binti al-dalīlati al-muḥtālati
sentences.l: So I said: I, I dislike that I marry with the like of you. So she said to me: If you married with me, you are-safe from the daughter of the Dalīla, the trickster.
sentences.i: I said, “I would not care to marry someone like you.” She said, “If you marry me, you will be safe from the daughter of Dalīla the trickster.”
sentences.n: in tazawwajta bī taslam, “if you married me, you are safe”: after in the past tense is a condition, and the jussive taslam is its result. bint al-Dalīla al-muḥtāla, “the daughter of Dalīla the trickster”: Dalīla is the name of a famous swindling old woman, and to call a woman her daughter is to call her a schemer of that breed. She means the lady ʿAzīz has been visiting.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا وَمَنْ بِنْتُ الدَّلِيلَةِ الْمُحْتَالَةِ فَقَالَتْ لِي وَقَدْ ضَحِكَتْ هِيَ الَّتِي لَكَ فِي صُحْبَتِهَا الْيَوْمَ سَنَةٌ وَأَرْبَعَةُ أَشْهُرٍ أَهْلَكَهَا اللَّهُ تَعَالَى وَابْتَلَاهَا بِمَنْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā wa-man bintu al-dalīlati al-muḥtālati fa-qālat lī wa-qad ḍaḥikat hiya allatī laka fī ṣuḥbatihā al-yawma sanatun wa-arbaʿatu ashhurin ahlakahā allāhu taʿālā wa-ibtalāhā bi-man huwa ashaddu minhā
sentences.l: So I said to her: And who (is) the daughter of the Dalīla, the trickster? So she said to me, and she had laughed: She (is) the-one who — for you in her company today (is) a year and four months. May God (exalted is He) destroy her and afflict her with (one) who is more-severe than her!
sentences.i: I said, “And who is the daughter of Dalīla the trickster?” She laughed and said, “She is the woman whose company you have kept for a year and four months now. May God Most High destroy her, and send her someone harder than herself!
sentences.n: allatī laka fī ṣuḥbatihā al-yawma sanatun, “the one for whom you have, today, a year in her company”: the length of time is the subject and laka the predicate, a common way of saying how long. ahlakahā allāhu, a past tense, is a curse: “may God destroy her”. ibtalāhā bi-man, “afflict her with one who”: bi- names the affliction.

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ مَا يُوجَدُ أَمْكَرُ مِنْهَا وَكَمْ قَتَلَتْ نَاسًا قَبْلَكَ وَكَمْ فَعَلَتْ أَفْعَالًا وَكَيْفَ سَلِمْتَ مِنْهَا وَلَكَ فِي صُحْبَتِهَا هَذِهِ الْمُدَّةُ وَلَمْ تَقْتُلْكَ أَوْ تُشَوِّشْ عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-allāhi mā yūjadu amkaru minhā wa-kam qatalat nāsan qablaka wa-kam faʿalat afʿālan wa-kayfa salimta minhā wa-laka fī ṣuḥbatihā hādhihi al-muddatu wa-lam taqtulka aw tushawwish ʿalayka
sentences.l: And by God, there is not found (one) more-cunning than her; and how-many she killed people before you, and how-many she did deeds! And how were you safe from her, and for you in her company this the period, and she did not kill you or trouble upon you?
sentences.i: By God, there is no one craftier than she is. How many people she has killed before you, and how many things she has done! How did you come through unharmed, all this time in her company, without her killing you or doing you some mischief?”
sentences.n: kam qatalat nāsan, “how many people she has killed”: after kam of exclamation the noun is normally genitive, but when a verb comes between kam and its noun, the noun goes into the accusative, as nāsan and afʿālan do here. shawwasha ʿalā, “to upset, make trouble for (someone)”, is spoken; the jussive tushawwish still follows lam, across aw, “or”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ كَلَامَهَا تَعَجَّبْتُ غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ فَقُلْتُ لَهَا يَا سَيِّدَتِي وَمَنْ عَرَّفَكِ بِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu kalāmahā taʿajjabtu ghāyata al-ʿajabi fa-qultu lahā yā sayyidatī wa-man ʿarrafaki bihā
sentences.l: And when I heard her speech, I wondered the utmost of the wonder, and I said to her: O my lady, and who made-you-acquainted with her?
sentences.i: When I heard what she said I was utterly amazed, and I said to her, “My lady, how do you come to know her?”
sentences.n: ghāyata al-ʿajabi, “the utmost of wonder”: an accusative that measures the verb. ʿarrafahu bi-, “to acquaint someone with”: the verb takes the person known with bi-.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ أَنَا أَعْرِفُهَا مِثْلَ مَا يَعْرِفُ الزَّمَانُ مَصَائِبَهُ لَكِنْ قَصْدِي أَنْ تَحْكِيَ لِي جَمِيعَ مَا وَقَعَ لَكَ مَعَهَا حَتَّى أَعْرِفَ مَا سَبَبُ سَلَامَتِكَ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat anā aʿrifuhā mithla mā yaʿrifu al-zamānu maṣāʾibahu lākin qaṣdī an taḥkiya lī jamīʿa mā waqaʿa laka maʿahā ḥattā aʿrifa mā sababu salāmatika minhā
sentences.l: So she said: I, I know her like what the time knows its calamities; but my aim (is) that you tell to me all of what befell you with her, so that I know what (is) the cause of your safety from her.
sentences.i: She said, “I know her as Time knows its own disasters. But what I want is for you to tell me everything that happened between you and her, so that I can learn how you escaped her.”
sentences.n: al-zamān, “Time”, the world’s course, is the bringer of misfortune in this literature: she knows the woman as well as Fate knows the blows it deals.

sentences.t: فَحَكَيْتُ لَهَا جَمِيعَ مَا جَرَى لِي مَعَهَا وَمَعَ ابْنَةِ عَمِّي عَزِيزَةَ فَتَرَحَّمَتْ عَلَيْهَا وَدَمَعَتْ عَيْنَاهَا وَدَقَّتْ يَدًا عَلَى يَدٍ لَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِمَوْتِ بِنْتِ عَمِّي عَزِيزَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥakaytu lahā jamīʿa mā jarā lī maʿahā wa-maʿa ibnati ʿammī ʿazīzata fa-taraḥḥamat ʿalayhā wa-damaʿat ʿaynāhā wa-daqqat yadan ʿalā yadin lammā samiʿat bi-mawti binti ʿammī ʿazīzata
sentences.l: So I told to her all of what happened to me with her and with the daughter of my paternal-uncle, ʿAzīza; so she asked-mercy upon her, and her two eyes shed-tears, and she struck a hand upon a hand, when she heard of the death of the daughter of my uncle, ʿAzīza.
sentences.i: So I told her everything that had passed between me and that woman, and between me and my cousin ʿAzīza. When she heard of my cousin ʿAzīza’s death she called down God’s mercy on her, her eyes filled with tears, and she struck one hand against the other.
sentences.n: taraḥḥamat ʿalayhā, “she asked mercy upon her”, saying “God have mercy on her”, as one does for the dead. Striking one hand on the other is a gesture of grief. samiʿat bi-, “she heard of”: bi- marks the news.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ شَبَابُهَا وَعَوَّضَكَ اللَّهُ فِيهَا خَيْرًا
sentences.tr: wa-qālat fī sabīli allāhi shabābuhā wa-ʿawwaḍaka allāhu fīhā khayran
sentences.l: And she said: In the way of God (is) her youth! And may God compensate you in her (with) good.
sentences.i: And she said, “Her youth, gone to God! May God give you something good in her place.
sentences.n: fī sabīli allāhi, “in the way of God”, is said over something lost: her youth is spent and gone, a lament for one who died young. ʿawwaḍaka allāhu fīhā khayran, “may God replace her for you with good”, is the condolence offered to the bereaved.

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ يَا عَزِيزُ إِنَّهَا مَاتَتْ وَهِيَ سَبَبُ سَلَامَتِكَ مِنْ بِنْتِ الدَّلِيلَةِ الْمُحْتَالَةِ وَلَوْلَا هِيَ لَكُنْتَ هَلَكْتَ
sentences.tr: wa-allāhi yā ʿazīzu innahā mātat wa-hiya sababu salāmatika min binti al-dalīlati al-muḥtālati wa-lawlā hiya la-kunta halakta
sentences.l: By God, O ʿAzīz, she died, and she (is) the cause of your safety from the daughter of the Dalīla, the trickster; and were-it-not-for her, you would have perished.
sentences.i: By God, ʿAzīz, she is dead, and it is she who saved you from the daughter of Dalīla the trickster. But for her, you would have perished.
sentences.n: wa-lawlā hiya, “were it not for her”: lawlā takes the free pronoun hiya here; la-kunta halakta, “you would have perished”, with la- marking what would have followed.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا خَائِفَةٌ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ مَكْرِهَا وَشَرِّهَا وَلَكِنْ فَمِي مَلْآنُ مَا أَقْدِرُأَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ
sentences.tr: wa-anā khāʾifatun ʿalayka min makrihā wa-sharrihā wa-lākin famī malʾānu mā aqdiru an atakallama
sentences.l: And I (am) fearful for you from her cunning and her evil, but my mouth (is) full; I am not able that I speak.
sentences.i: I have been afraid for you, of her cunning and her malice; but my mouth is full — I cannot speak.”
sentences.n: famī malʾānu, “my mouth is full”: she knows more than she will say. The print runs aqdir and an together as one word.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا إِي وَاللَّهِ قَدْ حَصَلَ كُلُّهُ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā ī wa-allāhi qad ḥaṣala kulluhu dhālika
sentences.l: So I said to her: Yes, by God, it has happened, all of it, that.
sentences.i: I said to her, “Yes, by God, all of that happened.”
sentences.n: ī, “yes”, is the yes used before an oath: ī wa-allāhi. kulluhu dhālika, “all of it, that”, is a loose order for kullu dhālika, “all that”.

sentences.t: فَهَزَّتْ رَأْسَهَا وَقَالَتْ لَا يُوجَدُ الْيَوْمَ مِثْلُ عَزِيزَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-hazzat raʾsahā wa-qālat lā yūjadu al-yawma mithlu ʿazīzata
sentences.l: So she shook her head and said: There is not found today the like of ʿAzīza.
sentences.i: She shook her head and said, “There is no one like ʿAzīza left in the world today.”

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ وَعِنْدَ مَوْتِهَا أَوْصَتْنِي أَنْ أَقُولَ لَهَا هَاتَيْنِ الْكَلِمَتَيْنِ لَا غَيْرُ وَهُمَا الْوَفَاءُ مَلِيحٌ وَالْغَدْرُ قَبِيحٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu wa-ʿinda mawtihā awṣatnī an aqūla lahā hātayni al-kalimatayni lā ghayru wa-humā al-wafāʾu malīḥun wa-al-ghadru qabīḥun
sentences.l: So I said: And at her death she charged me that I say to her these two the words, not other, and they two (are): The faithfulness (is) fine, and the treachery (is) foul.
sentences.i: I said, “And as she was dying she charged me to say these two sayings to that woman, and nothing more: ‘Faithfulness is fair, and treachery is foul.’”
sentences.n: The print has الوفاو, a misprint for الوفاء (al-wafāʾ, “faithfulness”), corrected here; the same saying is printed correctly a few pages earlier. lahā, “to her”, means the lady, not ʿAzīza. lā ghayru, “not other”, is “and nothing more”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ ذَلِكَ مِنِّي قَالَتْ لِي يَا عَزِيزُ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ هَاتَيْنِ الْكَلِمَتَيْنِ هُمَا اللَّتَانِ خَلَّصَتَاكَ مِنْهَا وَمِنَ الْقَتْلِ مِنْ يَدِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat dhālika minnī qālat lī yā ʿazīzu wa-allāhi inna hātayni al-kalimatayni humā allatāni khallaṣatāka minhā wa-mina al-qatli min yadihā
sentences.l: And when she heard that from me, she said to me: O ʿAzīz, by God, these two the words, they two (are) the two-which saved-you from her, and from the killing from her hand.
sentences.i: When she heard that from me she said, “ʿAzīz, by God, it was those two sayings that saved you from her, and from death at her hands.

sentences.t: وَالْآنَ قَدِ اطْمَأَنَّ قَلْبِي عَلَيْكَ مِنْهَا وَلَا بَقَتْ تَقْتُلُكَ فَقَدْ خَلَّصَتْكَ بِنْتُ عَمِّكَ حَيَّةً وَمَيِّتَةً
sentences.tr: wa-al-āna qadi iṭmaʾanna qalbī ʿalayka minhā wa-lā baqat taqtuluka fa-qad khallaṣatka bintu ʿammika ḥayyatan wa-mayyitatan
sentences.l: And now my heart has become-at-rest about you from her, and she no-longer remained killing you; for the daughter of your uncle has saved you, living and dead.
sentences.i: Now my heart is easy about you as far as she is concerned; she will not kill you now. Your cousin saved you, alive and dead.
sentences.n: wa-lā baqat taqtuluka, “and she no longer will kill you”: baqā (the spoken form of baqiya, “to remain”) with a verb after it means “to go on doing”, and with lā, “no longer”.

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي كُنْتُ أَتَمَنَّاكَ يَوْمًا بَعْدَ يَوْمٍ وَمَا قَدَرْتُ عَلَيْكَ إِلَّا فِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ حَتَّى تَحَيَّلْتُ عَلَيْكَ وَقَدْ تَمَّتْ عَلَيْكَ الْحِيلَةُ
sentences.tr: wa-allāhi innī kuntu atamannāka yawman baʿda yawmin wa-mā qadartu ʿalayka illā fī hādhā al-waqti ḥattā taḥayyaltu ʿalayka wa-qad tammat ʿalayka al-ḥīlatu
sentences.l: And by God, I was wishing-for you day after day, and I was not able upon you except in this the time, until I schemed upon you; and the trick has been completed upon you.
sentences.i: By God, I have longed for you day after day, and I could never get hold of you until now, when I laid a trap for you; and the trap has worked.
sentences.n: qadartu ʿalayka, “I had power over you”: to get hold of someone. taḥayyaltu ʿalayka, “I used a trick on you”, from ḥīla, a ruse; tammat ʿalayka al-ḥīla, “the ruse has been carried through on you”.

sentences.t: وَأَنْتَ الْآنَ غَشِيمٌ لَا تَعْرِفُ مَكْرَ النِّسَاءِ وَلَادَ وَاهِي الْعَجَائِزِ
sentences.tr: wa-anta al-āna ghashīmun lā taʿrifu makra al-nisāʾi wa-lā dawāhī al-ʿajāʾizi
sentences.l: And you now (are) raw; you do not know the cunning of the women, nor the calamities of the old-women.
sentences.i: And you are still a greenhorn; you know nothing of the cunning of women or the tricks of old women.”
sentences.n: ghashīm, “raw, inexperienced”, is a spoken word. dawāhī, “calamities”, are here the old women’s tricks. The print sets the space one letter too late, ولاد واهي, so that wa-lā, “nor”, takes the first letter of dawāhī; the reading is not in doubt, and the print’s spacing is kept.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَا وَاللَّهِ فَقَالَتْ لِي طِبْ نَفْسًا وَقَرَّ عَيْنًا فَإِنَّ الْمَيِّتَ مَرْحُومٌ وَالْحَيَّ مَلْطُوفٌ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lā wa-allāhi fa-qālat lī ṭib nafsan wa-qarra ʿaynan fa-inna al-mayyita marḥūmun wa-al-ḥayya malṭūfun bihi
sentences.l: So I said: No, by God. So she said to me: Be-good (in) soul and be-cool (in) eye, for the dead (is) shown-mercy, and the living (is) dealt-kindly with.
sentences.i: “No, by God, I do not,” I said. She said, “Take heart and be comforted: the dead are in God’s mercy, and the living in His kindness.
sentences.n: ṭib nafsan wa-qarra ʿaynan, “be good of soul and cool of eye”, are the stock words of comfort: a cool eye is a contented one, as a hot eye is a weeping one. malṭūfun bihi, “dealt kindly with”: laṭafa takes its object with bi-, and the passive keeps it.

sentences.t: وَأَنْتَ شَابٌّ مَلِيحٌ وَأَنَا مَا أُرِيدُكَ إِلَّا بِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ
sentences.tr: wa-anta shābbun malīḥun wa-anā mā urīduka illā bi-sunnati allāhi wa-rasūlihi ṣallā allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama
sentences.l: And you (are) a youth, handsome, and I, I do not want you except by the custom of God and His messenger, God bless him and give (him) peace.
sentences.i: You are a handsome young man, and I want you only in the way God and His Messenger allow — God bless him and give him peace.
sentences.n: bi-sunnati allāhi wa-rasūlihi, “by the custom of God and His Messenger”: in lawful marriage. ṣallā allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama is the blessing spoken after the Prophet is named.

sentences.t: وَمَهْمَا أَرَدْتَ مِنْ مَالٍ وَقُمَاشٍ يَحْضُرُ لَكَ سَرِيعًا وَمَا أُكَلِّفُكَ بِشَيْءٍ أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: wa-mahmā aradta min mālin wa-qumāshin yaḥḍuru laka sarīʿan wa-mā ukallifuka bi-shayʾin abadan
sentences.l: And whatever you wanted of wealth and cloth, it comes-present for you quickly, and I do not burden you with a thing, ever.
sentences.i: Whatever you want in money or fine stuffs will be brought to you at once, and I will never put you to any expense.
sentences.n: qumāsh, “cloth”, covers clothes and goods generally. kallafahu bi-, “to charge someone with”: bi- marks the cost or task laid on him.

sentences.t: وَأَيْضًا عِنْدِي دَائِمًا الْخُبْزُ مَخْبُوزٌ وَالْمَاءُ فِى الْكُوزِ
sentences.tr: wa-ayḍan ʿindī dāʾiman al-khubzu makhbūzun wa-al-māʾu fī al-kūzi
sentences.l: And also, with me always the bread (is) baked and the water (is) in the jug.
sentences.i: Besides, in my house the bread is always baked and the water always in the jug.
sentences.n: “The bread baked and the water in the jug” is a saying for a house where everything is ready to hand.

sentences.t: وَمَا أُرِيدُ مِنْكَ إِلَّا أَنْ تَعْمَلَ مَعِي كَمَا يَعْمَلُ الدِّيكُ
sentences.tr: wa-mā urīdu minka illā an taʿmala maʿī ka-mā yaʿmalu al-dīku
sentences.l: And I do not want from you except that you do with me as the rooster does.
sentences.i: All I want from you is that you do with me as the cock does.”

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا وَمَا الَّذِي يَعْمَلُهُ الدِّيكُ فَضَحِكَتْ وَصَفَّقَتْ بِيَدَيْهَا وَوَقَعَتْ عَلَى قَفَاهَا مِنْ شِدَّةِ الضَّحِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā wa-mā alladhī yaʿmaluhu al-dīku fa-ḍaḥikat wa-ṣaffaqat bi-yadayhā wa-waqaʿat ʿalā qafāhā min shiddati al-ḍaḥiki
sentences.l: So I said to her: And what (is) the-thing which the rooster does it? So she laughed, and clapped with her two hands, and fell on her nape from the intensity of the laughter.
sentences.i: I said to her, “And what is it that the cock does?” She laughed, clapped her hands, and fell over on her back, she laughed so hard.
sentences.n: ṣaffaqat bi-yadayhā, “she clapped with her two hands”: bi- of the instrument. waqaʿat ʿalā qafāhā, “she fell on the back of her neck”: flat on her back.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا قَعَدَتْ عَلَى حَيْلِهَا وَتَبَسَّمَتْ وَقَالَتْ لِي يَا نُورَ عَيْنِي أَمَا تَعْرِفُ صَنْعَةَ الدِّيكِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā qaʿadat ʿalā ḥaylihā wa-tabassamat wa-qālat lī yā nūra ʿaynī a-mā taʿrifu ṣanʿata al-dīki
sentences.l: Then she sat on her strength, and smiled, and said to me: O light of my eye, do you not know the craft of the rooster?
sentences.i: Then she sat up, smiled, and said to me, “Light of my eyes, don’t you know the cock’s trade?”
sentences.n: qaʿadat ʿalā ḥaylihā, “she sat on her strength”, is the spoken phrase for sitting up straight. ṣanʿa, “craft, trade”.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَا وَاللَّهِ مَا أَعْرِفُ صَنْعَةَ الدِّيكِ قَالَتْ صَنْعَةُ الدِّيكِ أَنْ تَأْكُلَ وَتَشْرَبَ وَتَنِيكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lā wa-allāhi mā aʿrifu ṣanʿata al-dīki qālat ṣanʿatu al-dīki an taʾkula wa-tashraba wa-tanīka
sentences.l: So I said: No, by God, I do not know the craft of the rooster. She said: The craft of the rooster (is) that you eat and drink and fuck.
sentences.i: “No, by God,” I said, “I don’t know the cock’s trade.” She said, “The cock’s trade is to eat, and drink, and fuck.”
sentences.n: tanīka, from nāka, yanīku, is the plain coarse verb for intercourse, and it is the young woman who uses it.

sentences.t: فَخَجِلْتُ أَنَا مِنْ كَلَامِهَا ثُمَّ إِنِّي قُلْتُ أَهَذِهِ صَنْعَةُ الدِّيكِ فَقَالَتْ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: fa-khajiltu anā min kalāmihā thumma innī qultu a-hādhihi ṣanʿatu al-dīki fa-qālat naʿam
sentences.l: So I was-ashamed, I, from her speech; then I said: Is this the craft of the rooster? So she said: Yes.
sentences.i: Her words made me blush. Then I said, “Is that the cock’s trade?” “Yes,” she said,

sentences.t: وَمَا أُرِيدُ مِنْكَ الْآنَ إِلَّا أَنْ تَشُدَّ وَسَطَكَ وَتُقَوِّىَ عَزْمَكَ وَتَنِيكَ جُهْدَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-mā urīdu minka al-āna illā an tashudda wasaṭaka wa-tuqawwiya ʿazmaka wa-tanīka juhdaka
sentences.l: And I do not want from you now except that you tighten your middle, and strengthen your resolve, and fuck your utmost.
sentences.i: “and all I want of you now is that you gird up your loins, stiffen your resolve, and fuck with all your might.”
sentences.n: shadda wasaṭahu, “to tighten one’s middle”, is to gird oneself for an effort. The print spells tuqawwiya with a final ى, as it often writes final yāʾ. juhdaka, “your utmost”, is an accusative of manner.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا صَفَّقَتْ بِيَدَيْهَا وَقَالَتْ يَا أُمِّي أَحْضِرِي مَنْ عِنْدَكِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā ṣaffaqat bi-yadayhā wa-qālat yā ummī aḥḍirī man ʿindaki
sentences.l: Then she clapped with her two hands and said: O my mother, bring-present whoever (is) with you.
sentences.i: Then she clapped her hands and said, “Mother, bring in the people you have with you.”
sentences.n: The print itself points man, “whoever”, so that it is not read min, “from”.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالْعَجُوزِ قَدْ أَقْبَلَتْ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهُودٍ عُدُولٍ وَمَعَهَا شُقَّةُ حَرِيرٍ ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا أَوْقَدَتْ أَرْبَعَ شَمْعَاتٍ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-ʿajūzi qad aqbalat bi-arbaʿati shuhūdin ʿudūlin wa-maʿahā shuqqatu ḥarīrin thumma innahā awqadat arbaʿa shamʿātin
sentences.l: And behold, (there was) the old-woman: she had come-forward with four witnesses, upright-ones, and with her a length of silk; then she lit four candles.
sentences.i: And there was the old woman, coming in with four upright witnesses and carrying a length of silk. Then she lit four candles.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-al-ʿajūzi, “and behold, the old woman”: after idhā of surprise, bi- only marks what appears. aqbalat bi-, “she came with”: bringing them. shuhūd ʿudūl are witnesses of good standing, whose word a judge accepts; a marriage contract needs them. A shuqqa is a length of cloth.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ الشُّهُودُ سَلَّمُوا عَلَيَّ وَجَلَسُوا فَقَامَتِ الصَّبِيَّةُ وَأَرْخَتْ عَلَيْهَا إِزَارًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala al-shuhūdu sallamū ʿalayya wa-jalasū fa-qāmati al-ṣabiyyatu wa-arkhat ʿalayhā izāran
sentences.l: And when the witnesses entered, they greeted upon me and sat; so the young-woman stood and let-down upon herself a wrap.
sentences.i: When the witnesses came in they greeted me and sat down, and the young woman rose and drew a veil-wrap down over herself.
sentences.n: An izār is the large wrap a woman puts on when men outside her family are to see her.

sentences.t: وَوَكَّلَتْ بَعْضَهُمْ فِي وِلَايَةِ عَقْدِ النِّكَاحِ فَكَتَبُوا الْكِتَابَ وَأَشْهَدَتْ عَلَى نَفْسِهَا أَنَّهَا قَبَضَتْ جَمِيعَ الْمَهْرِ الْمُقَدَّمِ وَالْمُؤَخَّرِ وَأَنَّ فِي ذِمَّتِهَا لِي عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: wa-wakkalat baʿḍahum fī wilāyati ʿaqdi al-nikāḥi fa-katabū al-kitāba wa-ashhadat ʿalā nafsihā annahā qabaḍat jamīʿa al-mahri al-muqaddami wa-al-muʾakhkhari wa-anna fī dhimmatihā lī ʿasharata ālāfi dirhamin
sentences.l: And she appointed some-of-them as agent in the guardianship of the contract of the marriage, and they wrote the writ; and she made-witness against herself that she had received all of the dower, the advanced and the deferred, and that in her charge (there are) for me ten thousands (of) dirham.
sentences.i: She appointed one of them as her agent, to stand as her guardian in making the marriage contract, and they wrote it out. Then before the witnesses she declared that she had received the whole of the dower, both the part paid at once and the part deferred, and that she owed me ten thousand dirhams.
sentences.n: A woman is given in marriage by a walī, a guardian, who makes the contract for her; she gives that office to one of the witnesses. The mahr, the dower a husband owes his wife, is paid in two parts, al-muqaddam when the contract is made and al-muʾakhkhar on divorce or death. By declaring she has received all of it, and that she owes him ten thousand dirhams besides, she frees ʿAzīz of every money claim and puts a debt on herself. ashhadat ʿalā nafsihā, “she made (them) witnesses against herself”: she bound herself formally. fī dhimmatihā, “in her charge”: as a debt she owes.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
